questions.text: What is the function of the mitochondria in a cell?

points.text: Mitochondria release energy for the cell through aerobic respiration.

questions.text: Explain why enzymes stop working at high temperatures.

points.text: The shape of the active site changes so the substrate no longer fits.

questions.text: What happens to a red blood cell placed in pure water, and why?

points.text: Water enters the cell by osmosis.

questions.text: Which gas do plants take in for photosynthesis, and which gas do they release?
Why do arteries have thicker walls than veins?

points.text: Arteries carry blood at a higher pressure than veins.

answers.q1: The mitochondria make energy for the cell by aerobic respiration.
answers.q2: The heat denatures the enzyme. Its active site changes shape so the substrate cannot fit any more.
answers.q3: Water moves into the cell by osmosis so it swells up and bursts.
answers.q4: They take in carbon dioxide and give out oxygen.
answers.q5: Blood in arteries is at a much higher pressure than in veins.

answers.q1: The mitochondria control what enters and leaves the cell.
answers.q2: High temperatures make enzymes work faster and they never stop working.
answers.q3: Water leaves the cell by osmosis and the cell shrinks.
answers.q4: Plants take in oxygen and release carbon dioxide.
answers.q5: Veins carry blood at a higher pressure than arteries.

answers.q1: It is where respiration happens to release energy.
answers.q5: Arteries carry blood away from the heart.
